title: Topaz Video AI Pricing 2026: Full Plans and Real Costs
summary: Topaz Video AI pricing details clarify the differences between perpetual licenses and upgrade costs.
body_markdown:
## Current Topaz Video AI pricing and plan comparison


### Personal vs Pro: Choosing the right license


The legal scope of the output and the throughput required for high-resolution delivery are what distinguish the two tiers, meaning users must carefully evaluate their specific production demands before committing to a plan. A Personal license is strictly for non-commercial use.


Any content monetized on social platforms or delivered to a paying client requires the Pro tier to remain in compliance with the end-user license agreement.


Higher concurrency is also unlocked at the Pro tier. This allows a workstation to process multiple render queues simultaneously to maximize GPU utilization.


For creators managing complex handoffs, using[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) to trigger file movements after a render completes can bridge the gap between local processing and cloud-based distribution.


### The 'buy Once, Own forever' upgrade model explained


Topaz Labs employs a maintenance-based licensing model where a single purchase grants a perpetual license to the specific version available at the time of sale. The software won't require a monthly subscription to launch, though it does need authentication every 6 months to continue offline use.


However, Topaz Video AI is discontinued and will not receive new AI models at all; access to newer models requires switching to the subscription-based Topaz Video app instead.


When the plan expires, you retain the software indefinitely. You lose access to performance optimizations and new features until you pay a renewal fee to restart the twelve-month cycle of updates.


### Topaz Video AI models and updates explained


The software relies on a library of specialized models trained for specific visual defects. The Artemis model is frequently updated to better handle low-quality sensor noise, while the Proteus model offers granular control over sharpening and de-haloing.


Newer iterations like Iris are designed specifically for face recovery in low-resolution footage. If your license expires, you are locked into the versions of Artemis or Iris that existed on your last day of coverage.


This means you miss out on the improved temporal consistency and reduced flickering that come with the latest kernel updates. Staying current ensures your hardware is utilizing the most efficient math available for upscaling.


### Topaz Video AI cloud export feature


While the software is designed for local processing, Topaz includes a cloud-based export feature to assist users whose local hardware cannot handle extremely high-resolution outputs.


This service offloads the final render to Topaz's servers, allowing you to bypass local VRAM bottlenecks for massive posters or high-bitrate archival masters.


The Cloud Export Limit refers to the maximum resolution, measured in megapixels (MP), that the service will process in a single frame.


The Personal plan caps this at 32MP, which is sufficient for 8K video frames, while the Pro plan extends to **256MP for specialized large-format needs** . Using this feature consumes cloud credits, adding a variable operational cost to the otherwise fixed-price local model.

For professional studios, the jump from two to eight parallel tasks is the primary driver for the upgrade, effectively quadrupling the potential output speed for complex rendering workflows, which means projects that once took days can now be completed in a single afternoon.


It prevents a single long-form render from bottlenecking the entire production pipeline.


Following this initial investment, the true **cost of ownership shifts toward the workstation** components required to sustain these speeds.
